system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Order: Markets, Tech Shock, and Regional Wars Collide
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, stressed system where technological disruption, market volatility and regional conflicts interact and amplify one another. AI-driven investment and cyber shocks are feeding financial stress (bond volatility, credit risk) even as energy and security shocks from the Middle East and Russia–Ukraine raise geopolitical tail risks. Major-power rivalry (US–China; US–Russia) and domestic political crises in Europe and emerging markets add feedback loops that make policy responses more constrained and outcomes more uncertain.
system_description.scope: State and non-state interactions shaping geopolitics and global stability: great-power competition, regional security crises (Middle East, Europe), global financial markets (bonds, credit, FX), energy and commodity flows, transnational tech and cyber ecosystems (AI, cloud providers, satellites), and major domestic political upheavals affecting international behaviour.
system_description.super_system: The integrated global socio-economic-political system (the international order linking states, markets, technology networks and transnational actors).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets (sovereign bonds, credit, FX and investor risk sentiment)
Energy and commodity markets (oil, shipping, strategic stockpiles)
Transnational technology & cyber ecosystem (AI buildout, cloud/neoclouds, satellite connectivity, major-platform governance)
Regional security complexes (Middle East conflict dynamics; Europe–Russia security dynamics)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine armed conflict
variables.description: Ongoing kinetic and diplomatic contest between Russia and Ukraine, punctuated by strikes, local ceasefires, prisoner swaps and intermittent U.S./Western mediation that continue to reshape front‑line dynamics and negotiation prospects.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology & supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: Strategic competition between the United States and China over advanced semiconductors, research links, export controls and industrial supply chains that is reallocating investment, talent and technological leadership worldwide.

variables.name: Iran–Gulf military and energy standoff
variables.description: An escalating regional confrontation involving Iran, Gulf states, proxy actors and U.S. forces marked by attacks on shipping, oil infrastructure and threats to undersea cables that elevate the risk of wider military escalation and energy‑market shocks.

variables.name: AI build‑out, market stress and cyber shock
variables.description: The rapid, capital‑intensive global roll‑out of frontier AI is driving credit and equity stress in neoclouds and vendors while AI‑enabled bugs and agents are triggering widespread cyber vulnerabilities and operational disruptions.

variables.name: France and eurozone sovereign bond stress
variables.description: Domestic unrest, fiscal strains and rising French yields are provoking contagion across eurozone sovereign markets and forcing a rebalancing of global safe‑haven flows and monetary‑fiscal responses.
